clue.text: They record earth-shaking events

parts.note: earth-shaking sounds like a figure of speech for momentous news, but here it is literal: instruments that log the ground's tremors

explanation.surface: A tribute to journalists or historians who chronicle world-changing happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth-shaking' invites the sense of sensational or historic; read literally it means earthquakes, and the things that record those are scientific instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: These instruments trace ground tremors on paper or screen, recording every earthquake.

clue.text: With not a single boy having revised lessons

indicators.note: revised means altered or reworked, so the letters of the word lessons are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A father with no male children goes over his lessons again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' looks like schoolwork being revisited but it is the anagram signal working on LESSONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any male child means having no boy at all; the suffix -less marks the absence.

clue.text: Getting in a good man this month

parts.note: a good man is a saint, abbreviated St as in St Paul

explanation.surface: Someone is welcoming a worthy fellow into the fold during the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: In old business letters the abbreviation for instant means 'of this month', as in 'your letter of the 5th inst'.
explanation.definitionFit: The commercial abbreviation of instant refers to the current calendar month in formal correspondence.

clue.text: Given permission, clear an area of London

parts.note: given permission means allowed, as in 'you may go'
fair weather is clear, cloudless weather

explanation.surface: Once permission is granted, a part of London is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: MAYFAIR is an upmarket district of central London, the priciest square on the British Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known wealthy district in the West End of the capital.

clue.text: Gormandiser's excess weight

definitions.note: read as 'gormandiser is', with the apostrophe s acting as the link to the wordplay

parts.note: an excess or oversupply is a glut
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A greedy eater's spare tyre of extra weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks possessive but stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gormandiser is someone who eats greedily, a synonym for a gourmand or overeater.

clue.text: A direction to be off!

parts.note: a way is a route or direction to go

explanation.surface: A command telling someone to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away!' is an order to be off; the surface's 'direction' doubles as an instruction and as a route.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off means absent or gone from a place, the same as not being present.

clue.text: Prevent the carrying out of capital punishment?

definitions.meaning: to prevent something is to intercept or forestall it before it arrives

definitions.text: the carrying out of capital punishment
definitions.meaning: read literally: beheading, removing the top of the body as an execution

explanation.surface: Someone stops an execution taking place.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: an execution by beheading takes the head off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means intercept or forestall; literally it describes decapitation, an old form of execution.

clue.text: A country gentleman's seat for occasional use

definitions.text: A country gentleman's seat for occasional use

parts.words: A country gentleman's seat for occasional use
parts.note: a country seat sounds like a grand estate, but here it is literally something to sit on, carried out on game days

explanation.surface: A rural squire's manor house that he visits now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'country seat' is normally a stately home; here it is a pointed walking stick whose handle unfolds into a small seat, used by spectators at field sports.
explanation.definitionFit: This walking stick unfolds into a perch for watchers at field sports, a gentry accessory.

clue.text: Professional person making possibly ten lads press on

indicators.note: possibly signals the words ten lads might be arranged another way

parts.note: to press on is to urge on, drive forward

explanation.surface: A professional encourages ten young men to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TEN LADS into DENTALS, then URGE ON follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth doctor who operates is a qualified practitioner, an example of a professional.

clue.text: Polish animal housing of reputable quality

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or polish
a sty is a pen housing pigs

explanation.surface: A Polish beast's lodging of respectable standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' masquerades as the nationality; it is the verb, to make smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Truthfulness and integrity are the virtue that makes someone reputable.

clue.text: Uninformed French article about a certain contention

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French article goes around the other pieces

parts.note: une is the feminine indefinite article in French
a war is a particular conflict or contention

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece on a dispute leaves readers in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article UNE, wrapped about A WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uninformed means lacking knowledge of something, being ignorant of it.

clue.text: Warning addressed to males only?

parts.note: O is the vocative exclamation used when addressing someone, as in 'O Lord'
a group of males only is men

explanation.surface: A caution aimed exclusively at the men in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O men!' would be a way to address an all-male audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or sign of what is coming serves as a warning of the future.

clue.text: Quiet workers making clothing

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
worker ants are the standard crossword workers

explanation.surface: Silent labourers turning out garments.
explanation.walkthrough: P for piano (quiet) is a music convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers or underpants are items of clothing, an example of the general category.

clue.text: Gulp and take flight

definitions.meaning: to swallow food hurriedly, as in wolfing a meal down
to run off suddenly, as a startled horse does

explanation.surface: Someone swallows nervously and runs away.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to swallow food hastily; the other is to flee suddenly.

clue.text: A break for key labour party members

parts.note: C is a musical key
the left wing of a socialist party, its members on the left

explanation.surface: A rift appears for the core members of the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like 'important', but it is the musical key C; 'labour party members' are the LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or fissure, a break in rock or a surface.

clue.text: Support a trainee, as is perfectly proper

parts.note: a leg is a support, as on a table
L is for learner, the L-plate on a trainee driver's car

explanation.surface: Backing an apprentice is entirely the right thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, so L stands for a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted by law is proper and above board.

clue.text: Detached in the main

definitions.meaning: aloof, cut off from others and narrow in outlook
literally, out in the main (the open sea), as an island is

explanation.surface: Mostly standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly'; the main is a poetic word for the open sea, where islands lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Island-like means both isolated in attitude and situated surrounded by sea.

clue.text: End fuel chaos — it's vital

indicators.note: chaos is disorder, so the letters of end fuel are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Stopping the fuel crisis is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' rearranges END FUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something necessary or required is essential, vital to have.

clue.text: The beast naturally looks down on others

definitions.text: The beast naturally looks down on others

parts.words: The beast naturally looks down on others
parts.note: looking down on others usually means snobbery; here the animal is simply taller than all others, by nature

explanation.surface: An arrogant brute who despises everyone around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks down on' suggests contempt; the tallest land animal literally looks down on everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The tallest living land animal sees over every other creature from its height.

clue.text: Proceed quickly with cereal production on Merseyside

definitions.note: a place by the Mersey: the clue names the area rather than the town itself

parts.note: to run is to proceed quickly
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Hurrying the grain harvest in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNCORN is an industrial town on the River Mersey, near Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This town stands on the south bank of the Mersey, in the region around Liverpool.

clue.text: Appeal for adjustment of rent, and scoff afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the eating piece after the rearranged rent
an adjustment of rent changes it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to scoff is British slang for to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A tenant asks for a rent review, then tucks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment of' turns RENT into ENTR; 'scoff' means eat, not mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal earnestly to someone is to beg or implore them.

clue.text: Many dislike a superior stately home

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
to hate is to dislike strongly
U means upper-class, superior, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Lots of people resent a grand, aristocratic mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' for upper-class comes from the British 'U and non-U' distinction in speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A French castle or country house is a grand residence, the equivalent of a mansion.

clue.text: Study only comfort

parts.note: to con is an old word for study or learn by heart
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: Reading is the one solace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' as study is old literary usage beloved of setters.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone in distress is to bring them comfort.

clue.text: Remove superseded brochure

parts.note: ex means former, superseded, as in ex-wife
a tract is a pamphlet or brochure

explanation.surface: Withdraw an out-of-date pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to pull it out, take it away.

clue.text: Note variation in the sound

indicators.note: a variation on the word note alters its letter order

explanation.surface: A musical variation in pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges NOTE; the musical surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone is the quality of a musical sound or voice.

clue.text: A trick to restrict growth

definitions.meaning: a daring feat or publicity trick
to stop something developing to its full size

explanation.surface: A ploy designed to hold back development.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a daring feat or ploy; the other is to check development or growth.

clue.text: A creature living in a long-past age

indicators.note: living in means dwelling inside, so the letters sit concealed within the words long-past age

explanation.surface: An animal that existed in some bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living in' looks like part of the definition but signals the hidden run inside LONG-PAST AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is an animal, a particular creature.

clue.text: Cut under a quarter, being blue

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the cutting piece below the quarter

parts.note: S is south, one of the four compass quarters
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Being cut by less than a quarter leaves someone depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under a quarter' suggests 'less than 25%', but in a down clue it places AXE beneath S, one of the compass quarters. Saxe blue is a light greyish blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxe is a pale greyish-blue colour, named after Saxony.

clue.text: Idle characters find a place selling convenience food

indicators.note: the characters, meaning letters, of idle are taken and put in a new order

explanation.surface: Lazy people locate a shop for ready meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle characters' looks like lazy people; it is the letters of IDLE, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods, ready to eat.

clue.text: Drink after church or render a hymn

indicators.note: after places the drink behind church and or

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: Have a pint after the service, or sing a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn tune, as in Lutheran church music.

clue.text: Duck with orange maybe as flavouring

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word orange could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Duck à l'orange, with a citrus flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O; 'maybe' rearranges ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb is used to flavour cooking, especially Italian dishes.

clue.text: He can make people lose all sense

definitions.text: He can make people lose all sense

parts.words: He can make people lose all sense
parts.note: losing all sense suggests driving people mad; literally it means removing all feeling, the doctor's job before surgery

explanation.surface: A man who drives everyone crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose all sense' suggests losing their minds; read literally, it is losing all sensation under a general anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctor administers drugs to remove all sensation from patients before operations.
